subject: CareSync PoC — deployment mode qualification & trial sprint plan
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@caresync.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: CareSync PoC — deployment mode qualification & next steps

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the time today — really useful conversation. I wanted to follow up with a concise recap and a proposed path for the PoC so we can lock stakeholders and timeline. Key notes from the call:

- Goal: Validate inference latency and auditability for PHI-containing documents (document extraction + redaction pipeline) at CareSync scale.
- Main constraint: security/compliance (HIPAA), prefer isolation.
- Preferred metrics to validate: p95 latency under typical batch sizes, sustained throughput (tokens/sec), and complete audit log of model inputs and outputs.

Three deployment modes to consider (short form):
1) Hosted API: fastest onboarding, lower ops burden, no customer-managed VPC; good for early functional validation but not ideal for PHI unless you opt for higher isolation controls.
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool in Redwood with stricter tenancy separation and SLA guarantees — lower latency variability, still managed by Redwood.
3) Private VPC / On-prem: customer-managed networking and control plane; meets most isolation/compliance needs for PHI.

Ask from our side to scope the PoC:
- Which deployment mode does CareSync prefer to validate in the pilot? (hosted/dedicated/private)
- Confirmation of success criteria (I listed three above) or any additions (encryption, key management, retention windows).
- Stakeholder list (CISO, infra owner, procurement contact) and preferred kickoff week.

I've attached the security questionnaire you mentioned (CareSync_Security_Reqs.pdf) for quick reference and we can align on any gaps.

Proposed PoC cadence if Private VPC is required (we can adapt if you prefer a different mode):
- Week 0: Kickoff + infra checklist (network peering, firewall rules, KMS access)
- Week 1: Private environment provisioning + baseline test harness
- Week 2: Ingestion and throughput testing; run representative prompts and monitor p95/p99
- Week 3: Security review, audit-log verification, handoff and decision meeting

Next steps: if you confirm Private VPC as the target we'll prepare a tailored PoC SOW and a runbook for your infra team. If you prefer Dedicated, we'll propose reserved capacity sizes and a similar 3-week validation plan.

Would you be available to confirm stakeholders and the target kickoff date later this week?

Thanks,

Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com

Attachments: CareSync_Security_Reqs.pdf
From: Maya Patel <maya@caresync.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@caresync.com>, CareSync IT <it@caresync.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CareSync PoC — deployment mode qualification & next steps

Connor,

Appreciate the clear summary. After syncing with Rajiv (infra) and our security team, CareSync would like to pursue the Private VPC option for the PoC — PHI handling and audit provenance are non-negotiable for the pilot.

Success criteria (high-level):
- Functional correctness: model outputs meet our redaction precision and entity extraction quality baselines (we will provide a small labeled test set).
- Performance: p95 latency for single-document extraction < 450ms for 2k token inputs; sustained throughput to handle 50 concurrent jobs at target batch sizes.
- Compliance: server-side encryption of data at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, KMS integration (we use AWS KMS), and immutable audit logs retained for 7 years.
- Observability: access to per-request latency/cost breakdown and exported traces for our SRE team.

Timelines: our internal target is a pilot kickoff the week of Feb 23 (we can stretch one week either way, but we need decision and contract terms this month).

Stakeholders:
- Maya Patel — Head of Product (maya@caresync.com)
- Rajiv Singh — Director, Infrastructure (rajiv.singh@caresync.com)
- Priya Menon — Compliance Manager (priya.menon@caresync.com)
- CareSync IT (it@caresync.com) — for network peering and firewall rules

I attached our security checklist; Rajiv will follow up with a short list of network/peering specifics.

Thanks,
Maya

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@caresync.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CareSync PoC — deployment mode qualification & next steps

Maya —

Thanks for the quick clarifications and the stakeholder list. Based on your constraints we propose the following PoC sprint plan for Private VPC specifically (three-week sprint):

Week 0 (prep, ~3 days):
- Finalize Statement of Work (SOW-draft-v1.docx attached).
- Exchange required IPs/subnets and KMS access; run a short network checklist with CareSync IT.
- Assign owners: Redwood infra lead (Laura Bennett) for environment provisioning; CareSync infra (Rajiv) for peering.

Week 1 (provision + smoke tests):
- Redwood provisions private control plane and the inference nodes in the agreed VPC.
- Run smoke tests with a small representative dataset (we'll provide a harness).

Week 2 (performance and functional):
- Full throughput and p95/p99 latency runs with representative workloads.
- Functional run against your labeled test set; collect quality metrics.

Week 3 (security & audit review):
- Validate KMS integration, encryption-at-rest, and audit-log exports.
- Joint review: decision gate meeting to accept PoC results or iterate.

Deliverables: SOW, infra runbook link (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcDEFgHIJk), test harness repo, and a short evaluation report covering latency, throughput, and compliance checks.

Risks / asks for CareSync:
- Timely procurement sign-off for any dedicated capacity or private control plane fees.
- Network team bandwidth to complete peering and firewall changes within the prep window.

If that cadence works, we'll circulate a calendar invite for kickoff and a final SOW for signatures. Connor/Laura will own delivery from Redwood.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Attachments: SOW-draft-v1.docx

Sounds good — confirm Feb 23 kickoff (Monday) and we'll block Rajiv and Priya for the prep meetings. Please send a calendar invite with the agenda and any pre-kickoff checklist items.

Thanks,
Maya
